title: Meta-CLIP: Metadata-Conditioned Contrastive Learning for Zero-Shot Disease Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.33674v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Medical vision--language pretraining learns transferable representations from paired images and radiology reports, yet differences in scanners and acquisition protocols can impair transfer. Existing approaches primarily enrich clinical semantics, leaving structured acquisition information in DICOM headers underused. We introduce Meta-CLIP, a metadata-conditioned contrastive framework that uses acquisition similarity to reweight cross-modal negatives during pretraining. A kernel over numerical and categorical DICOM fields defines a bounded pairwise margin. This margin increases the contribution of acquisition-similar negatives, emphasizing distinctions among studies that share imaging conditions. The kernel remains fixed during image--text optimization, and inference follows the standard dual-encoder architecture without requiring metadata. We evaluate Meta-CLIP on chest radiography and volumetric chest CT through zero-shot classification

translated_title: Meta-CLIP：基于元数据条件化对比学习的零样本疾病推断
translated_abstract: 医学视觉-语言预训练从配对的图像和放射学报告中学习可迁移的表示，然而扫描仪和采集协议的差异可能会损害迁移效果。现有方法主要致力于丰富临床语义，而DICOM头部中的结构化采集信息却未被充分利用。我们提出了Meta-CLIP，一种元数据条件化的对比学习框架，在预训练过程中利用采集相似性对跨模态负样本进行重新加权。基于数值型和分类型DICOM字段的核函数定义了一个有界的成对边际。该边际增加了采集相似负样本的贡献，强调了共享相同成像条件的研究之间的区分。该核函数在图像-文本优化过程中保持固定，推理时遵循标准的双编码器架构，无需元数据。我们通过零样本分类任务在胸部X光片和体积胸部CT上评估了Meta-CLIP。
tldr: Meta-CLIP提出了一种元数据条件化的对比学习框架，利用DICOM采集相似性对跨模态负样本重新加权以提升零样本疾病推断性能，且推理时无需元数据。
en_tdlr: Meta-CLIP is a metadata-conditioned contrastive learning framework that reweights cross-modal negatives using acquisition similarity from DICOM metadata to improve zero-shot disease inference, requiring no metadata at inference time.
